step1_analysis.description: A 6-transistor SRAM cell consisting of two cross-coupled inverters forming a bistable latch. In this extracted netlist, the access transistors (XM5, XM6) have their drain and source shorted to the internal nodes (likely an extraction artifact), so the circuit effectively operates as a standalone bistable latch.

paper_reference.title: 0.4-V Logic-Library-Friendly SRAM Array Using Rectangular-Diffusion Cell and Delta-Boosted-Array Voltage Scheme

standby_power.description: Power consumed by the cell in the hold state (WL=0).

sky130_expected.calculation: Leakage of 5um NMOS and PMOS is ~100pA total. 100pA * 1.8V = 180pW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on typical SKY130 Ioff of 10pA/um for 1.8V devices. The W=5um sizing in the netlist is unusually large for an SRAM cell, leading to higher leakage than a standard minimum-sized cell.

static_current_noise_margin_SINM.description: Maximum current the cell can source before flipping state, indicating stability against noise (extracted via N-curve).

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using the square law model for SKY130 NMOS. Represents the peak positive current in the N-curve.

write_trip_current_WTI.description: Maximum current required to force the cell to flip state, indicating write margin (extracted via N-curve).

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using the square law model for SKY130 PMOS. Value is negative as current flows into the node from the source.

trip_voltage.description: The voltage at which the internal inverter flips state.

sky130_expected.calculation: Inverter trip point with beta ratio ~5.4. Vtrip = (1.8 - 0.42 + 0.42 * sqrt(5.4)) / (1 + sqrt(5.4)) = 0.71V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the W/L ratios of the PMOS and NMOS transistors in the netlist.

step3_testbench.description: Measures standby power using an operating point analysis, and extracts the N-curve (SINM, WTI, and trip voltage) using a DC sweep on one of the internal nodes.
step3_testbench.spice:
* SRAM Cell N-Curve and Standby Power Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VWL WL 0 0
Vforce BL_L 0 0

XM1 BL_L BL_H VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 BL_H BL_L VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 BL_H BL_L GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 BL_L BL_H GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 BL_L WL BL_L GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 BL_H WL BL_H GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

.control
  * 1. Operating Point for Standby Power
  op
  let standby_power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print standby_power

  * 2. DC Sweep for N-Curve (Stability and Write Margin)
  dc Vforce 0 1.8 0.01
  * Current entering the node from the source
  let I_node = -i(Vforce)
  
  meas dc I_SINM max I_node
  meas dc I_WTI min I_node
  meas dc V_trip when v(BL_H)=0.9 fall=1
  
  quit
.endc
.end
